Fuel, fire, and moving air

Use Heat and Remaining fuel views to inspect the fire front. Automatic visual detail adjusts rendering cost as the scene gets busier. Choose an unburned forest to start your own experiment.

Ground fuel dries and heats before ignition. Sustained heat can ignite tree crowns. Wind, slope, moisture, rain, and landing embers shape how the fire spreads.

A dedicated worker runs Rust physics at fixed time steps, while the camera and interface stay independent. Smoke and embers respond to buoyancy, drag, turbulence, cooling, and dissipation. Three.js draws the resulting positions. Smoke can linger after you extinguish a fire.

This is an interactive physical approximation. The moving active region is 396 m across; altered trees pause outside it and retain their state when you return. The world and smoke reset on reload.
